objective.text: Describe flat shapes by their sides and angles.

explanations.title: Describe a shape without its name
explanations.text: You can describe a shape without saying its name. Count its sides. Count its corners. Are the sides straight?

explanations.title: What an angle is
explanations.text: Two sides meet at a corner. The shape they make there is called an angle. A shape with 3 corners has 3 angles.

source_ref.section: Concept Development: marking the angles

explanations.title: Build it on a geoboard
explanations.text: Make a shape on the geoboard with 4 sides. It can look different from mine. It still has 4 sides and 4 angles.

explanations.title: Different looks, same attributes
explanations.text: These shapes look different. But they all have 3 straight sides and 3 angles. They are all closed shapes.

misconceptions.label: Counting the same side or angle twice
misconceptions.description: Child counts one side or angle more than once while going around a shape, so the count is too big.
detection_signals: Gives a count larger than the number of sides shown (for example 10 for a 6-sided shape).
Says a different number for sides and for angles of the same polygon.
misconceptions.response_text: Let's count again. Put your finger on the first one. Stop when you get back to it.

source_ref.section: Concept Development: 'you won't count the same angle twice'; Student Debrief: Ethan counted 10 sides

misconceptions.label: Grouping by look instead of attributes
misconceptions.description: Child decides two shapes are different kinds because they look different, not by counting sides and angles.
detection_signals: Says shapes are not the same kind because one is bigger, longer or turned.
Does not mention the number of sides or angles when comparing.
misconceptions.response_text: Shapes can look different. Count the sides and angles. That tells us the kind of shape.

assets_required.why_this_method: Side and angle counts must be exact. Diffusion often draws wrong numbers of sides.
assets_required.description: Draws one polygon (or open figure) from a list of corner points. Can mark each angle with a small arc and number the sides.
must_show_exactly: Number of sides and corners exactly equals the question stimulus
Straight sides only, unless the stimulus asks for a curve
Open figures show a clear gap
Concave quadrilateral for q_pr_5 has exactly 4 sides and 4 angles, one angle opening outward
states_or_frames: count-around mode: sides or angles highlight one at a time
assets_required.interaction: Display. Optional tap to mark each counted side or angle.
